rows.note: This is the all-purpose spoken choice for encouraging someone or cheering a team on; use 安慰 for plain consolation and 氹 for cheering someone up.

example.english: We cheer for our teammates together.
example.jyutping: ngo5 dei6 jat1 cai4 tung4 deoi6 jau5 daa2 hei3

rows.note: Use this for the applauding part of cheering, when support is shown by clapping rather than words.

example.english: The audience cheer for the actors with applause.
example.traditional: 觀眾為演員精彩嘅演出鼓掌。
example.jyutping: gun1 zung3 wai6 jin2 jyun4 zing1 coi2 ge3 jin2 ceot1 gu2 zoeng2

rows.note: Use this casual verb when you cheer someone up or coax them into a happier mood.

example.english: That joke helped cheer me up.
example.jyutping: go2 go3 siu3 waa6 tam5 faan1 ngo5 hoi1 sam1

rows.note: Choose this when cheer means offering comfort or consolation to someone who is upset.

example.english: I went to cheer up my friend after a breakup.
example.traditional: 我去安慰下失戀嘅朋友。
example.jyutping: ngo5 heoi3 on1 wai3 haa5 sat1 lyun2 ge3 pang4 jau5
